title: 跟…相比, 比 + amount and 高我一头: compared with, three years older
explain: 跟 … 相比 'compared with …' puts the thing you compare against first, then says how the main subject differs: 跟去年相比，今年的雨多了 'Compared with last year, there is more rain this year'; 跟他相比，我的汉语差多了 'Compared with him, my Chinese is much worse'. 与 and 和 can replace 跟; 与 is the most formal.

In a 比 sentence, the amount goes after the adjective to say by how much: 他比我大三岁 'He is three years older than me'; 这本书比那本贵很多 'This book is much more expensive than that one'; 我比他高一点儿 'I am a bit taller than him'; 这条路比那条长五公里 'This road is five kilometres longer than that one'. Do not put 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence.

In speech the 比 can be left out when an amount follows: A + adjective + B + amount. 他高我一头 'He is a head taller than me'; 她大我三岁 'She is three years older than me'. It works with short adjectives such as 高, 大 and 早.

examples.zh: 跟去年相比，今年的雨多了。
examples.en: Compared with last year, there is more rain this year.

examples.zh: 跟他相比，我的汉语差多了。
examples.en: Compared with him, my Chinese is much worse.
He is three years older than me.
This book is much more expensive than that one.
He is a head taller than me.
She is three years older than me.

mistakes: 相比 needs 跟, 与 or 和 before the thing compared: 跟去年相比 is right; 去年相比 is wrong.
Do not put 很 before the adjective in a 比 sentence: 他比我很大 is wrong. Put the amount after it: 他比我大三岁.
Without 比 you need the amount: 她大我三岁, not 她大我.

q.en: He is three years older than me.
Compared with last year, there is more rain.

q.zh: 跟去年相比，今年的雨多了。
q.en: Compared with last year, there is more rain this year.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: This book is much more expensive than that one?
q.en: This book is much more expensive than that one.
q.explain: The amount goes after the adjective.

q.en: He is three years older than me.
q.explain: No 很 in a 比 sentence.

q.en: She is three years older than me.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is a head taller than me?
q.en: He is a head taller than me.
q.explain: The adjective comes first, the amount last.

title: 朵, 幅, 颗, 匹, 扇, 册 and 届: new measure words
formula: *朵 / 幅 / 颗 / 匹 / 扇
explain: Each noun has its own measure word, so learn the pair together. 朵 is for flowers and clouds: 一朵花 'a flower'. 幅 is for paintings, pictures and cloth: 一幅画 'a painting'. 颗 is for small round things such as stars, hearts and sweets: 一颗星星 'a star'. 匹 is for horses: 一匹马 'a horse'. 扇 is for doors and windows: 一扇门 'a door'.

册 is for volumes and copies of books: 第二册课本 'the second volume of the textbook'. 届 is for sessions, such as a competition, a meeting or a graduating class, and goes with 第 and a number: 第三届运动会 'the third sports meeting'. The sentence 墙上挂着一幅画 'A painting hangs on the wall' shows the usual order: place, verb, number, measure word, noun.

examples.en: There is a flower on the table.
A painting hangs on the wall.
He is riding a horse.
That door is open.

mistakes: Measure words are not interchangeable: a door is 一扇门, not 一朵门. Learn each noun with its measure word.
届 is only for sessions and classes (第三届), not for ordinary times: say 三次, not 三届, for 'three times'.

q.en: There is a flower on the table.
There are many stars in the sky.
A painting hangs on the wall.
q.explain: 幅 is the measure word for 画.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is riding a horse?
q.en: He is riding a horse.
q.explain: 匹 is the measure word for horses.

q.zh: 我们学校的第三届运动会开始了。
q.en: The third sports meeting of our school has started.
q.wrong: 我们学校的第三届个运动会开始了。
q.explain: 届 is already the measure word; do not add 个.

title: 性, 本, 之一 and 是否: -ness, this, one of, whether
explain: 性 after an adjective or a noun makes an abstract noun, like '-ness' or '-ity': 重要性 'importance', 安全性 'safety', 积极性 'enthusiasm', 可能性 'possibility'. 这件事的重要性不用多说 'The importance of this matter needs no more words'; 这个办法的可能性很小 'The chance of this method working is very small'.
本 'this, our' before a noun is formal and points to the speaker's own group or the current time: 欢迎来到本公司 'Welcome to our company'; 本月我们很忙 'This month we are very busy'.
之一 'one of' follows the group: 上海是中国最大的城市之一 'Shanghai is one of China's biggest cities'; 他是我最好的朋友之一 'He is one of my best friends'. The group before 之一 often has 最 or a number.
是否 'whether or not' is the formal form of 是不是 or 有没有 in an indirect question: 我不知道他是否同意 'I do not know whether he agrees'; 请告诉我你是否有空 'Please tell me whether you are free'. Do not add 吗 after it.

examples.zh: 这件事的重要性不用多说。
examples.en: The importance of this matter needs no more words.
Welcome to our company.

examples.zh: 他是我最好的朋友之一。
examples.en: He is one of my best friends.
I do not know whether he agrees.

mistakes: 是否 already asks the question, so do not add 吗: 我不知道他是否同意 is right; 我不知道他是否同意吗 is wrong.
之一 comes after the whole group. Say 上海是中国最大的城市之一, not 上海是之一中国最大的城市.

q.zh: 他是我最好的朋友之一。
q.en: He is one of my best friends.
Welcome to our company.

q.zh: 这个办法的可能性很小。
q.en: The chance of this method working is very small.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I do not know whether he agrees?
q.en: I do not know whether he agrees.
q.explain: 是否 goes before the verb.

q.en: Please tell me whether you are free.
q.wrong: 请告诉我你是否有空吗。
q.explain: 是否 already asks the question; do not add 吗.

title: Words you know, with a new meaning
explain: Some words you already know come back in HSK 5 with another meaning or another sound. The character is the same; the words around it tell you which one it is.

A new sound. 看 kān means 'to look after, to guard': 看家 'guard the house', 看门 'keep the door'; 看 kàn is 'to look'. 当 dàng means 'to treat as': 当作 'treat as', 上当 'be fooled'; 当 dāng is 'when, to be'. 倒 dǎo means 'to fall over': 摔倒 'fall down'; 倒 dào is 'to pour' or 'backwards'. 数 shǔ means 'to count': 数数 'count'; 数 shù is 'a number': 数字. 背 bèi means 'the back' and 'to recite': 背书 'recite a lesson', 背后 'behind'; 背 bēi is 'to carry on the back': 背书包. 好 hào means 'to like': 爱好 'hobby', 好奇 'curious'; 好 hǎo is 'good'. 行 háng means 'a row, a line of work': 行业 'industry', 银行 'bank'; 行 xíng is 'OK'. 量 liàng means 'amount': 数量 'quantity'; 量 liáng is 'to measure'. 为 wéi means 'to be, as': 成为 'become', 作为 'as'; 为 wèi is 'for'. 头 is neutral, tou, as a suffix: 木头 'wood', 石头 'stone', 里头 'inside'; on its own, 头 tóu is 'head'.

The same sound, a new meaning. 才 cái also means 'talent': 人才 'talented person', 天才 'genius'. 本 běn means 'this, one's own': 本月 'this month', 本地 'local'. 别 bié also means 'to part': 告别 'say goodbye', 分别 'part'. 喂 wèi means 'to feed': 喂鱼 'feed the fish'. 省 shěng means 'to save': 省钱 'save money'. 面 miàn means 'surface, side': 水面 'the water surface', 方面 'aspect'.

Five more come in pairs. 称 is chēng 'to weigh, to call' and chèn 'to match': 对称 'symmetrical'. 处 is chǔ 'to be in, to deal with' and chù 'a place, a point': 好处 'benefit', 到处 'everywhere'. 调 is diào 'to transfer, to investigate' and tiáo 'to adjust': 空调 'air conditioner'. 系 is jì 'to fasten' and xì 'a system, a department': 中文系 'the Chinese department'. 批 is pī 'a batch' and 'to approve'.

examples.en: Our dog can guard the house.

examples.zh: 请你数数这里有几本书。
examples.en: Please count how many books there are here.
You must be careful; do not be fooled.
He fell down.

mistakes: The sound is decided by the words around it: 看家 is kān but 看书 is kàn; 摔倒 is dǎo but 倒水 is dào; 数数 is shǔ but 数字 is shù.
头 after 木, 石 or 里 is neutral: 木头 mùtou. On its own, or in 头发, it is tóu, 'head'.

q.zh: 他每天早上在教室里背书。
q.en: He recites his lessons in the classroom every morning.
I want to save a little money.

q.zh: 孩子们对什么都很好奇。
q.en: Children are curious about everything.
q.explain: 好 hào = to like; 好奇 = curious.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He feeds the fish every evening?
q.en: He feeds the fish every evening.
This line of work is very hard.
q.explain: Do not put 是 before an adjective.

title: 哪怕…也…, 不是…还… and 不…不…
explain: 哪怕…，也… means 'even if, even though', and sounds stronger than 即使: 哪怕只有一天，我也想去 'Even if it's only one day, I want to go'; 哪怕再忙，我也会给你打电话 'No matter how busy I am, I will call you'.
不是…，还 / 还要… says the first thing is not enough on its own: 不是光有目标就可以，还要行动起来 'Just having a goal is not enough; you also have to act'.
不…不… is a short 'unless … not …': 不尝不知道 'You won't know unless you try it'; 这件事不做不行 'This has to be done'. 不见不散 'don't leave until we meet' is said when making a date.

examples.zh: 哪怕只有一天，我也想去。
examples.en: Even if it's only one day, I want to go.

examples.zh: 不是光有目标就可以，还要行动起来。
examples.en: You can't just have a goal; you also have to act.

examples.zh: 不尝不知道，这个菜真好吃。
examples.en: You won't know unless you taste it: this dish is really good.
Tomorrow at eight; I'll wait until you come.

mistakes: 哪怕 needs 也 (or 都) in the second part.
不见不散 is a fixed phrase for meeting up.

q.zh: 哪怕只有一天，我也想去。
q.en: Even if it's only one day, I want to go.

q.zh: 哪怕再忙，我也会给你打电话。
q.en: However busy I am, I will call you.
q.explain: 哪怕 + 再 + adjective, then 也.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Just having a goal is not enough; you also have to act?
options: 不是光有目标就可以，还要行动起来。
光有目标就可以，还要行动起来。
q.zh: 不是光有目标就可以，还要行动起来。
q.en: You can't just have a goal; you also have to act.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You won't know unless you try it?
q.en: You won't know unless you try it.
Tomorrow at eight; I'll wait until you come.
q.explain: 不见不散 when making a date.

title: More 被 and 把: 被他给洗坏了, 把书包一扔 and 墙上挂有
explain: In speech, 给 can go right before the verb in a 被 / 叫 / 让 sentence. It adds no new meaning but sounds more spoken: 我新买的衣服被他给洗坏了 'My new clothes got ruined in the wash by him'.
把 + thing + 一 + verb describes a sudden, quick action, usually followed by what happened next: 孩子把书包一扔，就跑出去玩了 'The child tossed his schoolbag down and ran out to play'.
把 + thing 1 + verb + thing 2 says what thing 1 was spent on or used for: 他把钱都买了衣服 'He spent all the money on clothes'.
Verb + 有 is a written way to say something is on a place: 墙上挂有一张地图 'A map hangs on the wall'; 桌子上放有一些书 'Some books lie on the table'. In speech, use verb + 着: 墙上挂着一张地图.

examples.zh: 我新买的衣服被他给洗坏了。
examples.en: My new clothes got ruined in the wash by him.

examples.zh: 孩子把书包一扔，就跑出去玩了。
examples.en: The child tossed his schoolbag down and ran out to play.
He spent all the money on clothes.
A map hangs on the wall.

mistakes: 给 goes right before the verb: 被他给洗坏了.
Verb + 有 is written style; in speech say verb + 着.

q.zh: 我的手机被他给弄坏了。
q.en: My phone got broken by him.
q.explain: 被 + doer + 给 + verb + result.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: The child tossed his schoolbag down and ran out?
options: 孩子把书包一扔，就跑了出去。
孩子把一书包扔，就跑了出去。
q.zh: 孩子把书包一扔，就跑了出去。
q.en: The child tossed his schoolbag down and ran out.
q.explain: 一 goes right before the verb.

q.en: He spent all the money on clothes.
q.explain: 把 + money + 买了 + what he bought.

q.prompt: Which sentence says (in written style): Some books lie on the table?
q.en: Some books lie on the table.

q.zh: 他把门一关，就哭了起来。
q.en: He shut the door and burst into tears.
q.explain: 把 + thing + 一 + verb, then what followed.

title: Spoken patterns (3): 用不着, 不管怎么说, 真有你的, 不看白不看
explain: 用不着 means 'there is no need to': 这么小的病，用不着去医院 'It's such a small illness; no need to go to hospital'.
X着也是X着 means 'since I'm … anyway, I might as well': 闲着也是闲着，我来帮你吧 'I've got nothing else to do anyway, let me help you'.
不管怎么说 means 'anyway, whatever you say': 不管怎么说，健康最重要 'Anyway, health matters most'.
真有你的 praises or teases someone for something clever or surprising: 真有你的，这么难的题都做对了 'You're amazing: you even got such a hard question right'.
不X白不X means 'it would be a waste not to': 票是免费的，不看白不看 'The tickets are free; it'd be a waste not to go'.

examples.zh: 这么小的病，用不着去医院。
examples.en: It's such a small illness; no need to go to hospital.

examples.zh: 闲着也是闲着，我来帮你吧。
examples.en: Since I'm free anyway, let me help you.

examples.zh: 不管怎么说，健康最重要。
examples.en: Anyway, health matters most.

examples.zh: 真有你的，这么难的题都做对了。
examples.en: You're amazing: you even got such a hard question right.

examples.zh: 票是免费的，不看白不看。
examples.en: The tickets are free; it'd be a waste not to go.

mistakes: 用不着 is casual; in writing say 不必 or 不需要.
不X白不X uses the same verb twice: 不看白不看.

q.zh: 这么小的病，用不着去医院。
q.en: It's such a small illness; no need to go to hospital.

q.zh: 不管怎么说，健康最重要。
q.en: Anyway, health matters most.
q.explain: 不管怎么说 at the start.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You're amazing, you even got such a hard question right?
options: 真有你的，这么难的题都做对了。
真你有的，这么难的题都做对了。
q.zh: 真有你的，这么难的题都做对了。
q.en: You're amazing: you even got such a hard question right.

q.zh: 票是免费的，不看白不看。
q.en: The tickets are free; it'd be a waste not to go.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I've got nothing else to do anyway, let me help you?
options: 闲着也是闲着，我来帮你吧。
闲也是闲着，我来帮你吧。
q.zh: 闲着也是闲着，我来帮你吧。
q.en: Since I'm free anyway, let me help you.

title: Spoken patterns (4): 打也打不得, 好是它坏也是它, 想来想去, 说什么就是什么
explain: X也X不得，Y也Y不得 describes being stuck, with nothing you are allowed to do: 对这个孩子他真没办法，打也打不得，说也说不得 'He really can't handle this child: he can't hit him and he can't scold him'.
X是它，Y也是它 means 'whether X or Y, this is the one; there is no other choice': 好是它，坏也是它 'Good or bad, this is it'.

X来X去，都是 / 还是… means 'after all the …ing, it is still …': 想来想去，还是这个办法最好 'After thinking it over and over, this is still the best way'; 听来听去，都是一些差不多的意见 'After hearing them all, they are much the same ideas'.
Verb + 什么就是什么 means 'whatever someone says goes': 父母说什么就是什么 'Whatever the parents say goes'.

examples.zh: 对这个孩子他真没办法，打也打不得，说也说不得。
examples.en: He really can't handle this child: he mustn't hit him and he mustn't scold him.
Good or bad, this is it.

examples.zh: 想来想去，还是这个办法最好。
examples.en: After thinking it over and over, this is still the best way.
Whatever the parents say goes.

mistakes: In X来X去 the same verb comes twice, 来 first: 想来想去.
These patterns are spoken and informal.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: You can't hit him and you can't scold him?
options: 打也打不得，说也说不得。
打也不得打，说也不得说。
q.zh: 打也打不得，说也说不得。
q.en: You mustn't hit him and you mustn't scold him.
Good or bad, this is it.

q.zh: 想来想去，还是这个办法最好。
q.en: After thinking it over and over, this is still the best way.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: After hearing them all, they are much the same ideas?
options: 听来听去，都是一些差不多的意见。
听去听来，都是一些差不多的意见。
q.zh: 听来听去，都是一些差不多的意见。
q.en: After hearing them all, they are much the same ideas.
Whatever the parents say goes.
